claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under sustained high-temperature loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr forms a high-entropy matrix with intrinsic lattice distortion.
Intrinsic lattice distortion promotes the formation of coherent nanoscale precipitates.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates act as dislocation sources.
Precipitate-dislocation interactions facilitate continuous dislocation glide.
Deformation of coherent precipitate structures suppresses local stress concentration and delays crack initiation.
Precipitate-dislocation interactions promote additional slip systems and more uniform plastic deformation.
Pure tungsten is dominated by limited slip and brittle fracture under the proposed conditions.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater ductility and fracture strain than pure tungsten.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness and energy absorption than pure tungsten.
A temperature range of 800–1200°C under sustained mechanical loading represents plasma-facing-component service conditions.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate under sustained high-temperature loading but is not asserted for room-temperature or transient loading.
The relative contributions of lattice distortion and precipitate coherence may vary with processing history and microstructure.
Matching grain size and processing history while applying identical temperature, environment, and load conditions provides a controlled comparison between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
The hypothesis is falsified if WTaTiVZr shows no statistically significant improvement in both plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten under identical high-temperature loading.
The hypothesis is falsified if coherent nanoprecipitates actively mediating dislocation dynamics are not observed.
